title: UMAMI: A Multimodal Benchmark Dataset for Evidence-Grounded Dietary Decisions
abstract: arXiv:2611.31068v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Dietary decisions require identifying a food's nutrient content and considering individual dietary needs, but recognizing food from an image alone does not provide this information. Visually similar foods can have different nutrient profiles, so selecting the wrong food record can lead to incorrect decisions even when nutrient rules are applied correctly. Furthermore, satisfying nutrient constraints does not necessarily establish a food's relevance to a person's intake. Evaluating these challenges together requires connecting food images, nutrient records, and individual intake histories. To support this evaluation, we introduce UMAMI (Unified Multimodal Assessment of Meals and Intake), a multimodal dataset and benchmark linking independently collected food images with nutrient profiles and respondent health and intake records. translated_title: UMAMI：面向基于证据的膳食决策的多模态基准数据集
translated_abstract: 膳食决策需要识别食物的营养成分并考虑个体的饮食需求，但仅凭图像识别食物无法提供这些信息。视觉上相似的食物可能具有不同的营养成分，因此即使营养规则应用正确，选错食物记录也可能导致错误的决策。此外，满足营养约束并不一定意味着该食物与个人的摄入相关。要综合评估这些挑战，需要将食物图像、营养记录和个人摄入历史关联起来。为支持这一评估，我们提出了UMAMI（膳食与摄入的统一多模态评估），这是一个多模态数据集和基准，将独立收集的食物图像与营养成分以及受访者的健康和摄入记录关联起来。利用该数据集，我们构建了三个诊断任务，涵盖视觉营养问答、个人……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出UMAMI多模态基准数据集，首次将食物图像、营养成分与个人健康及摄入记录关联起来，用于系统评估基于证据的膳食决策中的关键挑战。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces UMAMI, a multimodal benchmark dataset that links food images with nutrient profiles and individual health and intake records to systematically evaluate evidence-grounded dietary decisions.
